title: North Sea Aran blanket
subtitle: A 90 by 110 cm blanket in a complex Aran panel layout inspired by North Sea fisherman's ganseys.
excerpt: A 90 by 110 cm blanket in aran weight on 4.5 mm needles, featuring a gansey-inspired Aran panel layout: purl-ground moss diamonds, horseshoe cables, marriage lines, and seed-stitch anchor columns. About 900 g of aran wool. ADVANCED: seven simultaneous panel types with independent repeat cycles.
sourceNotes: The gansey stitch vocabulary (marriage lines, moss diamonds, horseshoe cables, seed-stitch anchor columns) is documented in Michael Pearson's Traditional Knitting (1984), §North Sea Ganseys, and Gladys Thompson's Patterns for Guernseys, Jerseys and Arans (1955). All individual stitch patterns are in the public domain; this blanket arrangement is an original combination.

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts × 26 rows = 10 × 10 cm in Aran cable pattern on 4.5 mm needles, blocked. The aran-weight gauge on 4.5 mm produces a denser, firmer fabric than on 5 mm.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cable pattern where two opposite-slanting crossings (one C4F and one C4B) are placed adjacently on the same row, creating an arch shape that resembles a horseshoe. The arch opens upward or downward depending on the placement order. Common in North Sea gansey patterns and British Aran knitting.

A gansey stitch pattern of paired diagonal lines worked in purl on a knit background, rising from the lower corners of a panel toward a central meeting point. The two lines cross at the top, symbolising the union of partners. Used in North Sea fishing community knitwear.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4.5 mm needles. The layout combines
horseshoe cables
marriage lines
, purl-ground moss diamonds, and seed-stitch anchor columns. Finished size: 90 cm wide by 110 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The North Sea Aran blanket is rated ADVANCED because it combines seven distinct stitch panel types, each with a different row-repeat cycle, operating simultaneously across the full width for the entire 286-row length. The purl-ground moss diamonds have a 12-row repeat; the horseshoe cables have a 6-row repeat; the marriage lines have an 8-row repeat; and the seed anchor columns are row-independent. Tracking all simultaneously requires a multi-row chart or dedicated row counters. Budget about 900 g (about 1,580 m / 1,730 yards) of 100% wool aran in natural or undyed. Traditional gansey patterns are always worked in undyed natural cream, navy, or smoke-grey. Buy in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 900 g (about 1,580 m / 1,730 yards) of aran-weight 5-ply or worsted-spun natural wool. Traditional gansey wool is tightly twisted; a smooth worsted-spun aran shows cable detail better than a bouncy woollen-spun.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4.5 mm (UK 7 / US 7) circular needle, 100 cm or longer

items.name: Row counters
items.qty: 3 (one per cable type with a different repeat cycle)

content.text: Gauge

20 stitches and 26 rows to 10 cm in Aran cable pattern on 4.5 mm needles, blocked. The tighter gauge on 4.5 mm (versus 5 mm) produces a denser, more traditional gansey fabric. Swatch the horseshoe cable and the moss diamond in adjacent columns for at least 15 cm to confirm gauge before casting on.

At 20 stitches per 10 cm, 90 cm requires 180 stitches. Panel layout across 180 stitches: [seed 4] + [horseshoe 12] + [seed 4] + [marriage-lines 16] + [seed 4] + [moss-diamond 24] + [seed 4] + [marriage-lines 16] + [seed 4] + [horseshoe 12] + [seed 4] + [remainder filled with moss diamond or plain knit purl ground] = 180 stitches total including adjustment for cable draw-in.
Stitches used

items.name: Horseshoe (12 sts)
items.qty: RS cable row: k2, C4B, C4F, k2, creates arch opening upward

items.name: Marriage lines
items.qty: 16-row repeat where purl diagonals rise from outer edges to meet at centre

items.name: Moss diamond
items.qty: 24-stitch, 12-row diamond in double-moss texture on a purl ground

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 180 stitches. Long-tail tail: (4.5 × 180) / 10 + 15 = 81 + 15 = 96 cm. Measure 115 cm of tail. Place panel markers after each zone boundary as you cast on. Reset all three row counters to 1.
Body

RS rows: work each panel according to its pattern chart, slipping markers. Advance counter 1 (horseshoe, 6-row cycle), counter 2 (moss diamond, 12-row cycle), and counter 3 (marriage lines, 8-row cycle) after each RS row. WS rows: work the reverse of each panel (k the purls, p the knits within each zone; seed stitches maintain their texture on WS by reading the stitch). When you set this aside, note all three counter positions.
Continue until the blanket measures 110 cm from the cast-on edge.
Stitch count check-ins

At row 143 (about 55 cm): count across all panels. You should have 180 stitches. Recount within each panel zone to isolate any error before continuing. At row 284 (about 109 cm): final count before casting off.
Common faults

Marriage lines losing their diagonal symmetry: the purl columns for both lines must advance by one stitch per RS row in opposite directions (one leaning left, one leaning right). If both are leaning the same way, one direction was reversed.

Moss diamond pattern losing definition after 20 rows: the 12-row repeat was miscounted and the diamond reversed too early. Use a dedicated row counter for this panel only; it does not share a cycle length with the other panels.

Multiple panels desynchronising after a mid-project break: three independent counters is the minimum. Write the counter state for all three on a sticky note before setting the work down. On resuming, verify the counter state against the current fabric appearance before knitting.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern with needles one full size larger (5.5 mm). Work slowly: the densely-patterned fabric is stiff and the cast-off benefits from pausing every 30 stitches to check the tension.
Finishing

Weave in all ends. Block with steam or by soaking: this is a traditional wool Aran and a wet block will open the cable panels and define the moss diamonds considerably. Pin to 90 × 110 cm and allow 48 hours to dry.
Care
Hand wash in cool water for traditional non-superwash wool aran. Squeeze gently, do not wring. Lay flat on a clean surface to dry, reshaping to dimensions. Traditional gansey wool felts in hot water.
What to try next

From a gansey-inspired blanket, try an actual gansey sweater next. Use the same stitch vocabulary, the same 4.5 mm needles, and the same aran wool. Work in the round from the hem to the underarm. Shape the shoulders with a traditional saddle. The techniques are the same; the construction changes from flat to circular.
